summary: Phase B (Communication) end-to-end testing — backend pytest 12/12 PASS, frontend Playwright flows 100% PASS. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_phase_b_comms.py covering presence (online list + directory excludes self with online flag), world chat (shape, profanity masking, 429 cooldown), admin moderation (list, soft delete hidden from /chat/world, mute => sender 403, unmute restores), messaging device gates (kiri email=403, kiri sms=200), threads + unread + 'message' notifications, reading thread marks-read (unread drops), reply threading (sms uses deterministic sms:lo:hi id, email respects thread_id), and block toggle (block=>403, unblock=>200). Frontend: as mara (phone+laptop) — chat-widget-open => chat-widget renders, chat-messages shows history, chat-input + chat-send posts message that appears live; nav-messages routes to /messages, messages-tab-sms / messages-tab-email both render, NO device-gate-banner for mara, compose-button opens compose-modal with compose-recipient/compose-body, compose-send dispatches and closes modal, thread-{id} opens ThreadView with thread-messages + thread-reply-input + thread-send + block-button, reply appears in thread, notifications-button + nav-messages-badge (showed '2') both render correctly. As kiri (phone-only) — SMS tab: NO gate banner, compose enabled; EMAIL tab: device-gate-banner present with copy 'You need a Laptop to send Email.' and compose-button correctly disabled. World Chat widget on /messages also visible with '4 online' count. time_scale untouched (=1.0).

minor.issue: Default subject fallback is '(no subject)' — fine, but if client sends an empty string subject for email the same fallback applies (string is non-None). Consider also setting fallback for whitespace-only subjects.

Toggle endpoint with no separate /unblock — the return field is {status: 'blocked' | 'unblocked'} which is correct, but a stateless caller cannot guarantee a desired end-state without first reading current state. Consider accepting an optional 'action' override ('block'|'unblock'|'toggle').

channel=all returns mixed sms+email threads with no channel filter on the response shape itself (channel is per-thread). Works, but UI must group; consider letting client request 'sms' or 'email' (already supported via query) — documented behaviour.
Returns 200 {ok:true} even when message_id does not exist (no matched_count check). Minor — consider 404 on unknown id for idempotency clarity.

issues: ChatWidget overlay on /messages partially covers the EMAIL Compose's right column / 'No Email yet' empty state when widget is open on smaller desktop widths; not blocking — widget has its own close button (chat-widget-close).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1663 lines (was ~1400 in iter_4). The split-into-routers recommendation is increasingly important — comms endpoints would map cleanly to /app/backend/routers/comms.py (chat, messaging) and /app/backend/routers/admin_chat.py.

comms.PROFANITY is hardcoded module-level and re-compiled per call (re.sub with re.escape). Pre-compile patterns at import time, or use a single alternation regex, to reduce CPU on hot chat path under load. Also the list is English-only and uses whole-word boundaries — substring/leetspeak (e.g. 'sh1t', 'f*ck') won't be masked. Acceptable for MVP; flag for future expansion.

POST /api/chat/world stores ts as ISO string but the cooldown comparison parses last_chat_at with parse_dt — fine, but every send does an O(N) update_one on players.id (no index hinted) AND inserts to world_chat. Index on world_chat.player_id + last_chat_at would help future moderation queries.

messages.deleted_by is an array — used for per-recipient soft-delete; no endpoint currently lets a user delete a message they received. Either remove the field or add a DELETE /messages/{id} that pushes player id onto deleted_by.

sms_thread_id uses 'sms:lo:hi' with lexicographic sort of UUIDs — deterministic and correct. However email thread_id is uuid4 on first send and the client must remember to pass thread_id on reply; if the client forgets, a NEW email thread is created. Frontend currently does this correctly in ThreadView, but the API contract should document the requirement (or accept (from,to,subject) for de-dup).
admin_chat_mute: minutes is max(1, body.minutes) — accepts huge values (e.g. minutes=999999999 → datetime overflow risk via timedelta). Add an upper bound (e.g. 60*24*365).

POST /api/messages/send notification body is truncated at text[:80] without an ellipsis and concatenates subject — at chat_max_length=2000 a notification body could still be 80+200 chars; minor formatting nit.

GET /api/messages/threads pulls up to 3000 messages and groups in Python — O(N) per-call cost grows with user history. Consider an aggregation pipeline with $group on thread_id and $sort once threads exceed a few thousand.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (chat-widget-open, chat-widget, chat-messages, chat-input, chat-send, nav-messages, nav-messages-badge, messages-tab-sms, messages-tab-email, device-gate-banner (kiri email only), compose-button, compose-modal, compose-recipient, compose-body, compose-send, thread-{id}, thread-messages, thread-reply-input, thread-send, block-button, notifications-button — all verified)
